summary: This article explains how a thin layer of gas high above Earth shields us from the sun's harmful rays, and how nations worked together to repair the damage people caused to it.
introduce: Show the title “The Ozone Layer: Earth's Sunscreen” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: a special gas made of three joined oxygen atoms that forms a protective layer high above Earth
a kind of light from the sun that people cannot see but that can harm skin and eyes
the layers of gas that surround a planet

challengeTerms.def: the layer of Earth's atmosphere above the one we breathe in, where most ozone is found
a group of atoms joined together, the smallest unit of a substance that keeps its properties
energy that travels through space as waves or rays

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a big environmental problem, once it starts, can never be fixed? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain what caused the hole in the ozone layer and how countries worked together to fix it.
struggling: Pre-teach ozone, ultraviolet, and atmosphere with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses stratosphere, molecule, and radiation to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
